text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kenyan Michael Odenyo, presumed dead in the Ethiopian Airlines plane crash, is alive but is currently under arrest in the Comoros after being mistaken for one of the three hijackers.

- A report published by the Oxford-based journal African Affairs says that local government in Kenya is in crisis and will remain so until "second- or third-rate politicians" who are only interested in using their positions as a "path to private wealth" are no longer in control.
- Oxfam, a British non-governmental organisation, warns that more than 330,000 people in Kenya's Eastern and North Eastern provinces will starve to death if the government does not act immediately.

- Friends of Democracy (FOD) pressure group says it is reluctant to endorse calls for an election boycott by the Raila-Matiba Opposition Alliance because it does not believe the ruling party will yield to constitutional reforms before the next general election.
- University of Nairobi students go on the rampage demanding the resignation of Higher Education Loans Board Secretary Professor Chacha Nyagoti Chacha.
- Officials of the Kenya Ports Authority report congestion at Mombasa's container terminal as three ships wait to unload.
- Local Government Minister William ole Ntimama promises to name Nairobi lawyers who have refused to remit to the City Council millions of shillings that they collected on behalf of the council.
- The Attorney-General's chambers rejects press reports that former cabinet minister Paul Ngei has been discharged from his bankruptcy by the High Court.
- Opposition members of parliament stage a walk-out from parliament after the government side moves an early closure to the debate on the Central Bank of Kenya Amendment Bill.
